newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Aug real earnings up 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Aug real earnings up 0.7 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, rose 0.7 percent in August, the Labor Department said Friday.
The August increase followed a 1.5 percent drop in July real average weekly earnings.

The August rise stems from a 0.3 percent rise in average weekly hours, a 0.5 percent increase in average hourly earnings and a 0.1 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers.
Real average weekly earnings in August were up 0.7 percent from August last year, the department said.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $256.17 in August, versus $254.29 in July and $254.34 in August 1995.
In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $408.33 in August, compared with $405.08 in July and $394.22 in August last year.
